project-management: Manage five-file project docs, trackers, GitHub issues and reviews.

# Project management

Resolve work from the current request, handoff and active tracker. Use verified repository facts and an existing local overlay; never hardcode an active epic or create an unnecessary overlay.

Keep each project under `docs/projects/<state>/<PREFIX>/` with AUDIT, PRD, ARCHITECTURE, DEVELOPMENT_PLAN and PROJECT_TRACKER. Complete an evidence-based audit and required baseline before code or other project documents. Continue existing projects in their existing files. Move the whole folder as status changes.

Track every blocker and append timestamp, actor, action, outcome and evidence to the tracker's final append-only Action Log. Preserve history. Archive only after all requested work and required verification are complete; do not defer remaining work without the user's instruction.

Read the document conventions and the relevant operating mode from the task index when planning, triaging, reviewing or verifying. Discover real test/deploy commands; synthetic checks do not prove production readiness. Vault changes use their owning CLI/API. Delegation requires authorization.
start: Start a session: verify shared runtime, summarize the repo, follow its local startup.

# Session start

Use the installed CLI or repository launcher. Run `startup-check ensure --json` (native `startup ensure --json` fallback), then `brief`. These start only missing configured managed services; brief is read-only. The bounded `scripts/start-session.mjs` wrapper implements this sequence.

Report transport health, authenticated brain access, daemon identity, SSSS tooling and app readiness separately. Unknown app configuration stays unknown. Never guess service commands, change credentials, restart a live process to hide a timeout or start sibling repos.

Follow a verified repo-owned start skill once. A shared copy of this workflow is not another startup step. Read the repo expert/entry page only when needed for the requested work. Report branch, active work, dirty state, freshness and material warnings briefly; fix a warning only when it blocks requested work. Load runtime diagnostics references only on failures.
cli-agents: Discover and coordinate authenticated terminal coding agents when delegation is authorized.

# CLI agents

Dispatch only with authorization. Discover installed binaries and verify account/subscription authentication, permissions and structured output before dispatch. Never inject provider API credentials as a substitute for subscription login.

Use the verified helper and stdin for prompts; inspect each CLI's actual argv/auth/parser contract. Keep task/repo/output scope explicit, bound concurrency and runtime, await owned workers and clean up. Treat process success, parsed results and runtime integration as separate evidence.

Read discovery/authentication and the chosen command contract before dispatch; read coordination only for fan-out. Read propagation before sharing this complete package. Preserve repo-specific overrides and unrelated skills; unsupported host adapters remain defects.
code-quality: Run the current repository's configured quality gates before delivery or after failures.

# Quality gates

Read the current repository's local quality skill and `config.json`; global methods do not define its stack or commands. Run its one-shot checker in background, then read the actual report and exit status. Use the configured sanctioned node and exclusive ownership lock; never start a continuous checker or reuse stale reports as verification.

Fix observed failures and recheck changed paths. Before delivery, use the required tier and verify the tested source matches the working source. Do not invent lint/typecheck commands. Report omitted tiers, failures and the limits of synthetic evidence. Consult checker/repair references only for the current operation.
skill: Create, audit and propagate portable skills while preserving repository ownership.

# Skill packages

Keep descriptions narrow and entrypoints brief. Put mode-specific detail in references and load only relevant sections. Scripts, assets and evals are optional when useful; this supersedes the historical requirement to create every resource directory.

Global skills contain portable methods; repo skills contain verified local facts. Declare scope explicitly, resolve physical aliases, verify local repository identity and never fan out repo-owned skills. Use the registered canonical owner and targeted CLI deployment; preserve local overrides and copy needed support files, not only SKILL.md.

For context maintenance, use `skill optimize` with explicit roots/packages. Default is dry-run; apply only lossless candidates. Oversized requirements, unknown ownership, drift or malformed input need review. Preserve original manuals, managed blocks, credentials and runtime state. Never use newest-copy sync to overwrite an authored source blindly.
research: Manage background research queues, status and retrieval through Total Recall.

# Background research

Use the configured Total Recall API/CLI and verify installed operations and authentication. Enqueue research only for a requested task or applicable authorized workflow; a queue acceptance is not completed research.

Keep source citations, confidence, freshness and conflicting evidence. Distinguish verified facts from inference and provider/adapter availability from actual results. Store memory through validated SSSS operations, never raw vault edits. Credentials stay in the secrets store.

Read queue/list/update/remove procedures for that operation. Read provider/crawling, synthesis or citation schema sections only when using or changing that path. Current source and runtime behavior override historical examples.
repo-expert: Map a codebase's ownership, architecture and behavior; verify its local expert.

# Repository expertise

Verify cwd, repository identity, manifest, Git state and the current request. Global expertise is a method; the repo-local expert owns implementation facts. Never import another repo's topology or overwrite a local expert with a generic copy.

Read the local expert entrypoint and only relevant architecture sections. Trace actual callers, mutations, authorization and runtime boundaries; names, plans and exit codes alone do not prove behavior. Confirm mutable facts against code/configuration.

For expert creation or regeneration, read initialization and the boundary procedure, preserve authored content and test repository identity. For audits, select the relevant mapping/behavior/reconciliation references; include source evidence and unresolved gaps.
security: Audit vulnerabilities or harden authentication, secrets and trust boundaries.

# Security

Use current repository code, configuration and applicable local guidance. Scope findings to evidence and realistic impact. Keep secrets out of chat, logs, argv, fixtures and published artifacts; resolve credentials through the supported store.

Read the audit workflow before an audit and the relevant remediation procedure before a fix. Verify auth/scopes, input/path boundaries, outbound requests and failure behavior where the changed path requires it. Do not turn routine work into an unrelated full audit.

Report actual findings, fixes, tests and remaining uncertainty. Provider acceptance, a manifest or synthetic result does not prove live secure operation. Preserve user authorization boundaries.
ssss: Validate or change SSSS schemas, operations, registries and portable host adapters.

# SSSS

Establish ground truth from the current composed registry, lock, installed validator and actual mutation path. Do not assume a proposed extension or operation exists. Read the applicable document/mutation contract before schema or persistent-state changes.

Use validated operation envelopes and the owning CLI/API; never silently fall back to raw canonical writes. Preserve identity, timestamps, append/lease/path safety, authorization and privacy boundaries. Verify registry with its lock and inspect validity, not just process exit.

Read workflow, bundles, localization, search or host-adapter sections only for those changes. Test valid and invalid inputs plus rollback/conformance. Local fixtures do not prove provider execution or portability.
test: Discover and run the current repository's relevant tests with truthful evidence.

# Tests

Read the current repo's local test skill, manifest and test configuration. Use real commands and the authorized test host; globals do not select another repository's framework. Run suites in background where required and inspect completion, exit code and actual results.

Cover meaningful changed behavior and edge cases; preserve mock/real separation. Verify the tested source matches the change. Clean owned fixtures, mock records and processes. Report failures or missing verification honestly; passing one spec does not certify a release.
code-mode: Inspect or change Code Mode sandbox, VFS and instruction-led execution.

# Code Mode

Inspect the current repository's actual sandbox, VFS, tool boundaries and host adapter before changing them. Do not assume examples describe a deployed integration. Keep instruction routing, execution permissions and persistent memory ownership explicit.

Read the sandbox procedure for execution changes, surface/tool integration for those paths, and validation before verification. Use supported SSSS operations for canonical state; do not bypass authentication or claim a sandbox boundary without implementation evidence.
meta-harness: Inspect harnesses, agent processes and mesh execution when authorized.

# Harness management

Resolve installed commands, authenticated accounts, permissions and recorded mesh access before execution. Dispatch or spawn agents only when authorized and supported by verified adapters. Read the selected CLI/process/mesh procedure; do not load every harness example.

Track owned processes, await work, inspect real results and clean up. A catalog entry is not proof of an available integration. Use validated memory operations and preserve repository boundaries.
plugins: Create, validate, install or share Total Recall plugins.

# Plugins

Use the plugin workspace and current `plugin.json`/extension contracts. Keep optional capabilities in plugins rather than portable memory core. Every claimed command, schedule, UI/API action or memory extension needs a real handler and validation.

Read implementation or installation references for that operation. Verify scopes, invalid input, canonical SSSS writes, failure reporting and actual execution. Sharing requires explicit authorization; public bundles exclude credentials, private vault content and runtime state. Read sharing procedures only when sharing is requested.

code-quality: Run Total Recall's configured package, registry and remote test gates.

# Total Recall quality

This repo uses Node ESM/Vitest; no tsc or ESLint commands exist. Read local `config.json`. Run one-shot `scripts/check.mjs` in background on the sanctioned test node and inspect `scripts/report.mjs` plus the fresh exit status. One checker owns the machine-wide lock.

Fast gates cover dist freshness, public/shipped paths, clean scaffold and locked SSSS registry. Tests are tier `remote`; `full` skips them. All suites/gates run on the sanctioned node. Preserve public generic paths and valid PID identity locks.

Before release, verify a native isolated backend health/version and the current dashboard build. Read release/pitfall references for daemon reload, isolation or diagnosis; never confuse server restart with daemon reload.
push: Prepare and publish a Total Recall npm/GitHub release when authorized.

# Total Recall release

Use this for package releases; ordinary feature commits use normal Git workflow. Read deploy ownership and the release checklist for this operation. Inspect current tree, canonical tracker, version and previous evidence before editing.

Use the sanctioned node for builds, suites and gates; verify immutable source/package identity, native isolated health/version, current frontend bundle and clean scaffold. Update changelog/package versions, verify registry artifact availability and preserve npmrc/credential safety. Never publish or claim delivery from stale gates.

Follow the verified auto-pull/deployment contract rather than inventing a deploy path. Keep external publication within the user's authorization; verify actual Git/npm outcomes and clean owned jobs.
security: Audit Total Recall secrets, API auth, rotation and outbound trust boundaries.

# Total Recall security

Read the relevant secrets, API, rotation, browser or egress procedure before changing that boundary. Never print secrets, redact after exposure, pass secrets in argv or copy browser sessions into published artifacts. Resolve credentials through the supported encrypted store and validated env/Keychain contract.

Rotation order: capture, shape-check, API-verify, store/export, then revoke old material. Only verified recipes may auto-click; manual classes stay human, high-risk providers retain their safety window. Preserve provider attribution and explicit authorization.

Require authenticated scoped REST access, safe paths/input, scoped subrouter auth, outbound policy and truthful failure states. Use isolated tests; synthetic success does not prove provider/browser behavior.

skill: Manage Total Recall skill registry, deployment and scoped propagation.

# Total Recall skills

Inspect `src/core/skills-registry.mjs` and supported CLI contracts for registry/deployment changes. Global methods and repository-specific expertise are separate owners. Declare scope, resolve aliases, verify repository identity and never blindly synchronize all skills.

Use targeted registry/deploy commands, protect `repo_scoped: true`, preserve local overrides and all needed package references/scripts. Never copy vault, credentials or runtime data as templates. Do not promote a foreign repository copy into a global source.

Use `skill optimize` for explicit package/root audits. Default dry-run preserves source; apply only verified lossless candidates. Authored summaries require review of essential constraints. Read deployment/contamination references only for those actions.
total-recall-project-management: Apply verified Total Recall planning and readiness differences.

# Total Recall project overlay

Use the shared project-management method for five-file lifecycle and final append-only Action Log. This overlay owns local differences, not active project state.

Core is portable memory/instructions; optional capabilities belong to plugins. SSSS is an external protocol/validator: verify composed registry and actual mutation contracts. Use this source CLI for vault writes; project Markdown is ordinary documentation.

Read relevant readiness/testing/release sections before verification or delivery. Actual manifest/configuration govern gates; no invented lint/typecheck. Suites/gates run in background on the sanctioned node. Native/provider/deployment claims need their own evidence; complete all requested work before archival.
okf: Check OKF compatibility when designing SSSS schemas.

# OKF compatibility

Read the official resources and SSSS relationship sections when designing or upgrading schemas. Verify current primary specifications instead of assuming historical examples are authoritative. Preserve semantic structure, portability and the composed SSSS registry/validation contract; keep host details outside portable schemas.
test: Run Total Recall unit, CLI, API and frontend tests.

# Total Recall tests

Use Vitest and actual `vitest.config.ts`; backend specs are co-located `.spec.mjs`, frontend specs use Testing Library. All suites run in background on the sanctioned test node. Inspect source identity, completion and exit status; clean fixtures/mock writes and owned jobs.

Read cross-cutting suites before search, embeddings, context dispatch or proposal lifecycle changes. Test meaningful failure cases and complete SSSS properties. No browser alert() dialogs. Synthetic results do not certify live integrations or releases.
